statement: Directly replace repeated native target tensor-parallel All-Reduce barriers with SiFAR speculative reduction to improve current TP1/DP4/EP4 decode latency.
mechanism: Dual-buffer payload/validation, in-switch redundant pull and speculative readiness verification.
rejection_scope: Direct transfer to the current planned TP1 serving path; not a claim the method never helps TP deployments.
source_observation: Unversioned URL fetched; exact observed fulltext hash retained.
grounding: Paper explicitly focuses on TP and evaluates within a Megakernel, not vLLM runtime.
Target TP group world_size1 all_reduce returns input; native fused mHC allreduce requires TP4 and no EP.
Expert all-to-all and occasional embedding parallel-group reductions are different paths and do not establish repeated TP payload exposure.
Paper §8.1 explicitly admits false-pass stale payload if relative progress reverses between data and validation reads.
partial_reuse: Dual buffering with a rigorously proven lifetime/order contract may be reusable in a future real collective; speculative top-barrier removal is not accepted without stronger validation. No new positive card from this batch.
CPU_evidence: flag_validation_counterexample.json symbolic source-described ordering, no hardware reproduction.
baseline: c455786 Flash1017 planned TP1/DP4/EP4, live equivalence unknown
reopen_when: A separate target with actual repeated eligible allreduce, measured exposed cost, legal switch path and correctness protocol proven beyond monotonic-progress assumption.
